question: I'm a full-time federal employee with 2 years of service. How much annual leave do I earn each pay period?
answer: You earn one-half day of annual leave for each full biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)].
gold_answer: 4 hours (½ day) per biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(1)]

question: I've worked full-time for the government for 4 years. How many hours of annual leave do I get per pay period?
answer: For full-time employees with 3 but less than 15 years of service, annual leave accrues at 6 hours for each full biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)].
gold_answer: 6 hours (¾ day) per pay period; 10 hours in the last full pay period of the year [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)]

question: How much annual leave per pay period does a full-time employee with 16 years of service earn?
answer: One day for each full biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(3)(ii)].
gold_answer: 8 hours (1 day) per pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(3)]

question: How many hours of annual leave does a full-time employee with 4 years of service earn in a whole year?
answer: A full-time employee with 4 years of service earns 6 hours of annual leave for each pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)].

question: What is the maximum amount of annual leave most federal employees can carry over into the next leave year?
answer: Most federal employees can carry over a maximum of 30 days of annual leave into the next leave year [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Ceilings].
gold_answer: 240 hours (30 days) [5 U.S.C. 6304(a)]

question: How much annual leave can a federal employee stationed overseas carry over?
answer: Federal employees stationed overseas may carry over up to 45 days of annual leave [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Ceilings].
gold_answer: 45 days (360 hours) [5 U.S.C. 6304(b)]

question: What is the annual leave carryover limit for Senior Executive Service members?
answer: Senior Executive Service members have an annual leave carryover limit of 90 days [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Ceilings].
gold_answer: 90 days (720 hours) [5 U.S.C. 6304(f)]

question: How fast does a full-time federal employee accrue sick leave?
answer: A full-time federal employee accrues sick leave at a rate of one-half day for each full biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6307(a)].
gold_answer: 4 hours (½ day) per biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6307(a)]

question: Is there a cap on how much sick leave I can accumulate?
answer: There is no limitation on the amount of sick leave that can be accumulated [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information) > Sick Leave Accumulation].
gold_answer: No, there is no limit on accumulated sick leave [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information)]

question: How many hours of sick leave can I use in a leave year for general family care or bereavement?
answer: Up to 104 hours (13 days) of sick leave for general family care and bereavement each leave year [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information) > Sick Leave Usage Limits per Leave Year].
gold_answer: Up to 104 hours (13 days) per leave year [5 CFR 630.401(b)]

question: How much sick leave can I use to care for a family member with a serious health condition?
answer: An employee is entitled to use up to 12 weeks (480 hours) of sick leave each leave year to provide care for a family member with a serious health condition [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave to Care for a Family Member with a Serious Health Condition > Sick Leave Entitlement].
gold_answer: Up to 480 hours (12 administrative workweeks) per leave year [5 CFR 630.401(c)]

question: How much FMLA leave is a federal employee entitled to?
answer: Covered Federal employees are entitled to a total of 12 workweeks of unpaid FMLA leave during any 12-month period [5 U.S.C. 6382(a)(1)].
gold_answer: 12 administrative workweeks in any 12-month period [5 U.S.C. 6382(a)(1)]

question: How much paid parental leave can a federal employee take after the birth of a child?
answer: Up to 12 administrative workweeks of Paid Parental Leave (PPL) [OPM fact sheet: Paid Parental Leave > Introduction].
gold_answer: 12 administrative workweeks of paid parental leave [5 U.S.C. 6382(d)(2)]

question: How many days of leave can I get to donate bone marrow?
answer: Up to 7 days of leave [5 U.S.C. 6327(b)(1)].
gold_answer: Up to 7 days [5 U.S.C. 6327(b)(1)]

question: How much leave is available to a federal employee who donates an organ?
answer: Up to 30 days of paid leave [5 U.S.C. 6327(b)(2)].
gold_answer: Up to 30 days [5 U.S.C. 6327(b)(2)]

question: What is the maximum disabled veteran leave a new employee can be credited?
answer: A new employee can be credited with up to 104 hours of disabled veteran leave [5 U.S.C. 6329(a)].
gold_answer: Up to 104 hours [5 U.S.C. 6329(b)(1)]

question: What is the most sick leave an agency can advance to an employee?
answer: The most sick leave an agency can advance to a full-time employee is 240 hours (30 days) [5 CFR 630.402(b)].
gold_answer: Up to 240 hours (30 days) [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information)]

question: Under the Emergency Leave Transfer Program, how much donated annual leave can one recipient receive at a time?
answer: An emergency leave recipient may receive a maximum of 240 hours of donated annual leave at any one time from an ELTP for each disaster or emergency [5 CFR 630.1111].
gold_answer: Up to 240 hours per disaster or emergency at any one time [OPM fact sheet: Emergency Leave Transfer Program]

question: If I scheduled annual leave in advance but got sick and couldn't use it before the year ended, can it be restored?
answer: Annual leave scheduled in advance may be restored if forfeited due to sickness only if the leave was scheduled before the start of the third biweekly pay period prior to the end of the leave year [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Importance of Scheduling "Use or Lose" Leave in Advance].
gold_answer: Yes, annual leave lost because of sickness when scheduled in advance is restored [5 U.S.C. 6304(d)(1)(C)]

question: What is the 2026 annual salary for GS-12 step 5 in the Washington-Baltimore locality?
answer: The provided policy documents do not cover this.
gold_answer: $116,071 [OPM 2026 GS pay tables, DCB]

question: What is the overtime hourly rate for a GS-12 step 5 in the Washington DC area in 2026?
answer: The overtime hourly rate for a GS-12 step 5 in the Washington DC area in 2026 is 1.5 times the employee's hourly rate of basic pay [5 U.S.C. 5542(a)(2)].
gold_answer: $55.89 per hour [OPM 2026 GS pay tables, DCB]

question: What does a GS-9 step 1 earn per year in the Rest of U.S. locality in 2026?
answer: A GS-9 step 1 in the Rest of U.S. locality in 2026 earns $84,638 [5 CFR 531.214(d)(2)].
gold_answer: $61,722 per year; $29.57/hour [OPM 2026 GS pay tables, RUS]

question: Which federal holidays fall in December 2026?
answer: Christmas Day (December 25) [OPM fact sheet: Holidays Work Schedules and Pay > Holidays for Federal Employees].
gold_answer: Christmas Day, Friday 25 December 2026

question: What date is Thanksgiving in 2026 for federal employees?
answer: Thanksgiving Day is on the fourth Thursday in November, which in 2026 falls on November 25 [OPM fact sheet: Holidays Work Schedules and Pay > Holidays for Federal Employees].
gold_answer: Thursday 26 November 2026

question: I'm part-time with 5 years of service and had 52 hours in a pay status this pay period. How much annual and sick leave did I earn?
answer: For part-time employees with 5 years of service, you earn 1 hour of annual leave for each 13 hours in a pay status. With 52 hours in a pay status, you earned 4 hours of annual leave [5 CFR 630.303]. The provided policy documents do not cover sick leave accrual rates for part-time employees.
gold_answer: 4 hours annual (52/13) and 2.6 hours sick (52/20) [5 U.S.C. 6303(a); 6307(a)]

question: I have 4 years of service, full-time, and 250 hours of annual leave at the end of the leave year. How many hours will I lose if I don't use them?
answer: You will lose 155 hours of annual leave [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Entitlement].
gold_answer: 10 hours would be forfeited (250 − 240 cap) [5 U.S.C. 6304(a)]

question: Do I get extra pay for regularly scheduled night work, and how much?
answer: Yes, you get extra pay for regularly scheduled night work, which is a 10 percent differential of your basic pay rate [5 U.S.C. 5545(a)] [5 CFR 550.121(a)].
gold_answer: Yes, a night differential of 10% of basic pay for regularly scheduled work between 6 p.m. and 6 a.m. [5 CFR 550.121(a)]

question: What premium pay do I get for working on a Sunday as part of my regular schedule?
answer: You are entitled to Sunday premium pay equal to 25 percent of your rate of basic pay for each hour of Sunday work [5 U.S.C. 5546(a) and 6128(c)].
gold_answer: Basic pay plus 25% premium pay for each hour of Sunday work [5 CFR 550.171(a)]

question: For a non-exempt employee, at what rate is overtime paid under the FLSA and when does it start?
answer: Overtime pay is at one and one-half times the employee's hourly regular rate of pay, starting after 8 hours in a day or 40 hours in a workweek [5 CFR 551.501(a)(6)].
gold_answer: 1.5 times the regular rate for hours over 8 in a day or 40 in a workweek [5 CFR 551.501(a)]

question: How many hours is the basic workweek for a full-time federal employee?
answer: The basic workweek for a full-time federal employee is 40 hours [5 CFR 610.111(a)(1)].
gold_answer: 40 hours, not over more than 6 of any 7 consecutive days [5 CFR 610.111(a)(1)]

question: How long do I need to have worked for the government before I can use FMLA leave?
answer: An employee must have 12 months of qualifying civilian or military service [OPM fact sheet: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) 12-Week Entitlement > 12 Months of Qualifying Civilian or Military Service].
gold_answer: At least 12 months of service [5 U.S.C. 6381(1)(B)]

question: Can I take compensatory time off instead of being paid for irregular overtime?
answer: Yes, you may take compensatory time off instead of being paid for irregular or occasional overtime work, provided it is approved by the agency head or designee [5 CFR 550.114(a) to 550.114(b)].
gold_answer: Yes, at the employee's request the agency may grant compensatory time off instead of overtime pay [5 CFR 550.114(a)]

question: What is the maximum recruitment incentive as a share of annual basic pay?
answer: The maximum recruitment incentive as a share of annual basic pay is 25 percent [5 CFR 575.109(b)(1)], unless waived for a critical agency need, in which case it may be up to 50 percent [5 CFR 575.109(c)(1)].
gold_answer: Generally up to 25% of annual basic pay for the service period [5 CFR 575.109(b)(1)]

question: What is the maximum retention incentive an individual employee can be authorized?
answer: The maximum retention incentive for an individual employee is 25 percent [5 CFR 575.309(a)], unless a waiver is approved, which may allow up to 50 percent [5 CFR 575.309(e)(1)].
gold_answer: 25% of basic pay for an individual employee [5 CFR 575.309(a)(1)]

question: I'm at GS step 2. How long must I wait for my next within-grade increase?
answer: For an employee at GS step 2, the waiting period for the next within-grade increase is 52 calendar weeks [5 CFR 531.405(a)(2)(i)].
gold_answer: 52 calendar weeks of creditable service (steps 1–3) [5 CFR 531.405(a)]

question: How long is the waiting period between step 5 and step 6?
answer: The waiting period between step 5 and step 6 is 104 weeks [OPM fact sheet: Within-Grade Increases > Required Waiting Periods].
gold_answer: 104 calendar weeks (steps 4–6) [5 CFR 531.405(a)]

question: How long is the wait for a within-grade increase once I'm at step 7 or above?
answer: The waiting period for a within-grade increase once at step 7 or above is 156 calendar weeks [5 CFR 531.405(a)(2)(iii)].
gold_answer: 156 calendar weeks [5 CFR 531.405(a)(iii)]

question: What is the most administrative leave an agency can place an employee on in a calendar year?
answer: An agency may place an employee on administrative leave for no more than 10 workdays in a calendar year [5 U.S.C. 6329a(b)(1)].
gold_answer: No more than 10 work days per calendar year [5 U.S.C. 6329a(b)(1)]

question: When does the federal leave year begin?
answer: The federal leave year begins on the first day of the first full biweekly pay period in a calendar year [OPM fact sheet: Leave Year Beginning and Ending Dates > Fact Sheet: Leave Year Beginning and Ending Dates].
gold_answer: On the first day of the first full biweekly pay period in the calendar year [OPM fact sheet: Leave Year]

question: If my office closes for a snowstorm, can my agency give me paid leave?
answer: Yes, an agency may approve paid weather and safety leave if employees are prevented from safely traveling to or performing work at an approved location due to a snowstorm [5 U.S.C. 6329c(b)(1) to 6329c(d)(2)].
gold_answer: Yes, weather and safety leave without loss of pay may be approved [5 U.S.C. 6329c(b)]

question: Do I have to agree to keep working for my agency after taking paid parental leave?
answer: Yes, you must agree to work for your agency for not less than 12 weeks after paid parental leave concludes [OPM fact sheet: Paid Parental Leave > Advanced Written Service Agreement].
gold_answer: Yes, you must agree in writing beforehand to work for the agency for at least 12 weeks after the leave ends [5 U.S.C. 6382(d)(2)]

question: Is there a minimum length of service to be eligible for paid parental leave?
answer: An employee must have a continuing parental role and meet FMLA eligibility requirements, which include at least 12 months of qualifying Federal service [OPM fact sheet: Paid Parental Leave > Key Features of PPL].
gold_answer: Yes, at least 12 months of service before the birth or placement [5 U.S.C. 6382(d)(2)]

question: I'm GS-12 step 5 in the Washington DC area. How much overtime pay do I earn for 2 hours of overtime in 2026?
answer: For 2 hours of overtime, your overtime pay would be 1.5 times your hourly rate of basic pay [5 U.S.C. 5542(a)(2)].
gold_answer: 2 × $55.89 = $111.78 [OPM 2026 GS pay table (DCB)]
